studies.label: Phase 2: story writing with optional persona-generated AI plot ideas (Prolific)

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 43, Story writing by participants (recruitment and random assignment); PDF p. 11, Section 3.1 (analyzed counts)
counts_source.quote: 100 participants were recruited on Proliﬁc, ... we analyzed 97 stories: 32 in the control group, 33 in the 1-plot condition, and 32 in the 5-plot condition.

arms.name: 0-plot (control, human only)
arms.description: Wrote a story without AI support; excluded participants who reported external AI assistance in the post-task control verification. PDF pp. 10-11, 45-46.

arms.name: 1-plot
arms.description: Could request one plot idea randomly selected from the pre-generated persona pool; requesting and using the suggestion were optional. PDF pp. 10-11, 43, 47-48.

arms.name: 5-plot
arms.description: Could request up to five plot ideas randomly selected from the pre-generated persona pool; requesting and using the suggestions were optional. PDF pp. 10-11, 43, 49-51.

studies.task: Write an eight-sentence English story about an adventure on another planet for a teenage and young adult audience (PDF pp. 10-11 and participant interfaces, pp. 45-51).

ai_tool.name: GPT-4o (version 2024-05-13) on Azure OpenAI, using personas developed with ChatGPT o1-preview
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 5, Section 2.1; PDF pp. 29-30, Developing the ten diverse personas and Prompting the personas for plot ideas. PDF p. 11 links these pre-generated ideas to the human experiment.

preregistration.where: No preregistration for this experiment is stated in the full manuscript or appended Supplementary Materials.

estimates.outcome: Story similarity to the condition centroid
estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: Cosine similarity between each story embedding and the mean embedding of all stories in its own assigned condition; OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002. Scores are scaled to 100 (PDF p. 7), with one story per participant. PDF p. 11, Section 3.2; PDF p. 52 identifies the embedding model. Higher scores mean greater between-writer homogeneity.

stats.difference_is: The regression coefficient is treatment minus control on the printed similarity scale.

regression.model: Linear regression of story-to-condition-centroid cosine similarity on assigned-condition indicators, with the human-only condition as reference; fitted to all analyzed stories.

estimates.outcome: Pairwise story similarity within condition (crossed-story mixed model)
estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: Within-condition pairwise cosine similarity of story embeddings from OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002, scaled to 100 (PDF p. 7). Analysis uses every pair of stories within an assigned condition, with crossed random intercepts for both stories in a pair. Each participant wrote one story; PDF pp. 11 and 13, Sections 3.2 and 3.3.2.

stats.difference_is: The mixed-model coefficient is treatment minus control on the printed similarity scale.

regression.model: REML linear mixed model: similarity ~ condition + (1|story1_id) + (1|story2_id); condition is a fixed effect and both stories in each pair receive random intercepts.

sources.locator: PDF p. 52, Table S2, Bayesian Model Summary, residual parameter

estimates.notes: The interval fields contain the explicitly printed Bayesian highest-density interval, not a frequentist confidence interval. The test object (type other) contains BF01, the Bayes factor for null versus alternative, not a t/z statistic or p-value. The reverse Bayes factor BF10 is retained in the same source quotation. The paper does not specify the Bayesian analysis unit or enough hierarchy detail to confirm the independence basis; se_basis=not_reported denotes this missing basis, while the posterior interval itself is reported. The participant arm counts refer to the analyzed assigned-condition sample; no separate Bayesian exclusions are stated. The two-arm total is not separately printed and is null. No frequentist SE is inferred from a posterior SD or HDI. The model-summary source quotation gives mean, posterior sd, and the two HDI endpoints. It prints the lower HDI endpoint at lower precision than the Equivalence Testing block, which supplies the interval fields. control_mean is the posterior intercept; the fitted treatment mean is not printed and has not been derived. The intercept quotation also preserves its posterior sd and HDI; these are not a control-arm outcome SD or frequentist SE. Additional posterior probabilities are preserved in the Equivalence Testing source quotation. These probabilities are not frequentist p-values; their labels are retained exactly. The ROPE definition is quoted separately; no equivalence statistic is transformed. The sigma summary is preserved as a model parameter quotation, not an arm-level SD.

open_items: The publisher version is not on file. The extraction uses the saved accepted manuscript and its embedded supplement; the supplied citation record identifies a later journal version.
Per-arm randomized counts are not printed. Only total recruitment/random assignment and post-exclusion arm counts are reported; no arm allocation counts have been reconstructed.
Table 2 does not label its parenthesized values or specify the SE method. Those values are retained verbatim in source quotes; regression SEs remain null pending confirmation.

Table S3 gives story-average means and Cohen's d but no arm SDs/SEs, no standardizer definition, and no pairwise degrees of freedom. The printed t and d signs use the reverse order of the extraction treatment/control labels.
The main-text story-level omnibus ANOVA and the Table S3 omnibus F disagree. Both quotations are retained; neither is assigned to a pairwise estimate.

The Bayesian response unit and hierarchy are not explicitly described. The screening form suggests story-level averages by arithmetic, but that inference is not used to assign an otherwise unprinted unit here. The posterior uncertainty is reported; its participant-level independence basis cannot be confirmed.

Table S2 prints the Bayesian lower HDI endpoints at different precision in its model-summary and equivalence-testing blocks. The more precise explicitly printed equivalence-testing endpoints are transcribed, and the summary rows are retained in the sources.
The formation and counts of the NLTK analysis groups in Tables 5-6 are not reported consistently with the assigned arms. These contrasts remain excluded in accordance with the reconciled form.
Actual requests for and use of the optional AI plots are not reported. Eligible contrasts estimate assigned access to the ideas.

No preregistered primary outcome or single primary similarity analysis is named. The centroid, crossed-story pairwise, story-average, and Bayesian specifications share the same human sample and are not independent experiments.
notes: Extraction B. The complete markdown conversion was read in contiguous chunks through its end, including references and Supplementary Materials. Tables, figures, appendix materials, and participant-interface screenshots were inspected in the PDF; cited numerical pages were checked with PyMuPDF text extraction and table recovery. Study identifiers are retained from the reconciled screening form: only S2 is eligible; model-only S1 is listed under not_extracted. The analysis inventory comprises three centroid comparisons (including the descriptive AI-design comparison), two crossed-story mixed-model coefficients, three story-average robustness comparisons, and three Bayesian contrasts. Additional omnibus, distribution-summary, model-parameter, and posterior-probability statistics are preserved in contextual source quotations with empty fields; they are not alternative pairwise effects. Power targets for hypothetical future samples are not outcome contrasts. No estimates are read from unlabelled plots, and no values, totals, SDs, differences, or standard errors are calculated. Per-arm counts are people. n_total stays null where no two-arm total is separately printed; the printed full-model n_units values are explicitly identified in their records. The paper analyzes one story per participant after removing control participants who reported outside AI use; the control-only verification appears in the supplement. Table S3's Intent-to-Treat label does not remove those documented exclusions. All recorded outcomes concern between-writer similarity with AI access offered during writing; higher values mean more similar outputs. The original signs, comparison order, and printed precision remain visible in the source quotations. Posterior SDs, HDIs, ROPE probabilities, and Bayes factors are distinguished from frequentist SDs, SEs, confidence intervals, and p-values. There is no reported shared participant sample with Doshi and Hauser; that paper's Table 2 comparison column is not re-extracted. The paper has no rated-creativity outcome or reported after-AI outcome.
